s:
Arrange the following temples of Ellora in chronological order according to their time of construction :

I. Ravan ki Khai

II. Kailasanatha

III. Dashavatara

IV. Dumar Lena
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (IV, I, III, II); it is added as option 5.
Dhumar (Dumar) Lena, Cave 29, is one of the earliest Ellora excavations (6th century, Kalachuri period). Ravan ki Khai (Cave 14) was begun before the Dashavatara (Cave 15, with Dantidurga's inscription of c. 753–57), and the Kailasa (Cave 16, Krishna I) came last. So the order is IV, I, III, II, which no printed option gives. The printed key (III, I, IV, II) is wrong on two counts: it puts the Dashavatara before Ravan ki Khai and Dumar Lena third.

s: To which period do the sites of Ellora and Elephanta belong?
x:
Most books and keys: Rashtrakuta period. Strictly: many art historians date the main Elephanta cave to the mid-6th century (Kalachuris), with Ellora begun before the Rashtrakutas (PMF Art & Culture; Wikipedia, Elephanta Caves).
Standard books (PMF, Rocket) credit the art of both Ellora and Elephanta to the Rashtrakuta period; the Pratiharas and Hoysalas had nothing to do with them.

s: During whose reign were the Elephanta Caves constructed off the Mumbai coast?
x:
Most books and keys: Rashtrakutas. Strictly: many historians date the main cave to the mid-6th-century Kalachuris, before both Chalukya and Rashtrakuta rule in the Konkan (PMF Art & Culture; Wikipedia, Elephanta Caves).
NextGen Rocket and PMF credit the Elephanta caves to the Rashtrakutas; the Satavahanas and Pratiharas did not build them.

s: Which of the following statements about the Elephanta Island is correct?
o: It was given its name by the British after a large elephant structure located there.
It is well-known for a spectacular carving of Vishnu described in the Vishnudharmottara Purana.
It is associated with the Pashupata sect.
x: Elephanta's Great Cave is a Shaiva shrine linked with the Pashupata sect (Lakulisha is carved there). The Portuguese, not the British, named it after a stone elephant; it has seven caves, not one; and its famous carving is the Shiva Trimurti, not Vishnu.

s: Which of the following caves is famous for ‘Trimurti’?
x: The Trimurti (Sadashiva/Maheshamurti), a three-headed Shiva, is the masterpiece of Elephanta; Ellora is famous for Kailasa.

s: The Elephanta caves were mainly sculptured for which of the following devotees?
x: The Elephanta caves are mainly Shaiva shrines (Trimurti, Nataraja, Ardhanarishvara); only two small caves are Buddhist.

s: Which one among the following religions was partronised by Rashtrakutas?
x: Jainism got the Rashtrakutas' special patronage: Amoghavarsha I followed Jinasena, Jain poets filled their courts and about a third of the Deccan was Jain. The early kings were also Shaivas (Kailasa), but the keyed answer for this question is Jainism.
